prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system: River Intake Pump Station–High Service Pump Header; excludes distribution. Aliases: River Intake Pump Station=Ironwood; Coagulant Dosing Skid=Marigold; North Filter Gallery=Cobalt; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench=Sparrow; SCADA Historian Server=Lantern; Maintenance Planner=Quarry. Intake requires withdrawal/demand/depth limits/permissives; losses alarm/stop. Raw Water Screen Channel sends postcleaning Rake Torque Snapshot; rapid changes require verification; Maintenance Planner compares loading before rake-work release. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode, targets/responses/return-stability, urgent dosing/sampling; reviews deviations/recovery and next-day capacity/quality/demand. Storm sampling increases until raw/settled stability. Coagulant Dosing Skid sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies identity. Feedback loss requires verified safe/fixed dosing/grabs. Duty Engineer approves temporary turbidity/configuration changes, reconciles field/laboratory differences, checks maintenance constraints/may defer work. North Filter Gallery records scan turbidity/headloss; South Filter Gallery sends Filter Run Exception Note. Runs/backwash consider upstream conditions; return requires rinse-to-waste targets/stability. Overrides require justification/monitoring/restoration; maintenance preserves filtration capacity. Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench receives custody-controlled samples; sends checked Jar Test Photograph Set. Laboratory Technician sends complete Sample Chain Slip; verifies acceptance/custody, records mismatches. Late/warm samples: troubleshooting-only. Release requires analytical checks; failures require correction/rejection. Field results remain provisional pending matched laboratory reconciliation; notify Chief Operator of unsupported adjustments. SCADA Historian Server retains synchronized trends/accepted-result timestamps. Chlorine Contact Basin residual alarms require assessment/grabs; chemical work requires ventilation/monitoring/communications. Sample Backwash Recovery Tank after consequential returns. Clearwell Level Controller changes coordinate header plans. Work orders require approved windows/responsibility/return conditions, equipment/isolations/parts/closure-evidence. Identify all energy hazards; craft verifies isolation locally; operations acknowledges. Ironwood release requires tags/verification/turnover acknowledgment. Shifts communicate isolations/limits/unavailability/abnormalities. Chemical Supplier Driver sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; routes/areas/times restricted, operator observes; coagulant-transfer hoses/containment/washdown inspected. Residuals Hauler removes residuals. Distribution Dispatcher receives demand/production notices and advance header/North Distribution Pressure Station/South

New part:
S118: When Storm Intake Mode is active, discretionary work is reviewed again because debris loading, chemical demand, and operator workload may change quickly.
S119: A Chlorine Residual Alarm during maintenance causes the affected task to pause until operations confirms whether the alarm is process-related or maintenance-induced.
S120: The Laboratory Technician supports work control by confirming sampling needs and by reporting any acceptance concern that could delay equipment return.
S121: The Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench remains available for maintenance-related samples when water quality confirmation is required before a unit is returned to service.
S122: Evidence for return to service may include local inspection results, functional test readings, instrument response checks, sample results, and operator acceptance comments.
S123: Equipment is returned to service only after temporary jumpers, bypasses, tools, spare parts, and barriers have been removed or formally accepted for continued use.
S124: If a post-maintenance test fails, the work order stays open and the Chief Operator determines whether the equipment remains isolated or can be operated under restriction.
S125: The SCADA Historian Server retains operating data needed to compare pre-work and post-work performance for pumps, dosing systems, filters, and level controls.
S126: Following maintenance closeout, disinfection control is returned to normal service only after the Chief Operator confirms that the chlorine feed controls, residual instruments, and level indications are responding consistently in the SCADA Historian Server.
S127: The Chlorine Contact Basin is operated to maintain the required contact time under the current production rate, basin level, and measured disinfectant residual.
S128: Operators adjust chlorine feed gradually so that changes in residual do not outrun mixing and contact time through the Chlorine Contact Basin.
S129: When a Chlorine Residual Alarm occurs, the control room verifies analyzer sample flow, compares the reading with a grab sample result, and holds any planned production increase until the condition is understood.
S130: The Laboratory Technician provides confirmatory residual results when analyzer drift, sample line fouling, or an unexpected residual trend is suspected.
S131: The Clearwell Level Controller maintains normal storage within established operating limits that protect disinfectant contact, reserve volume, and high-service pump suction conditions.
S132: Low clearwell level interlocks are configured to prevent pump operation from drawing the storage volume below the minimum level needed for safe hydraulic operation.
S133: High clearwell level alarms give operators time to reduce production or adjust downstream pumping before overflow conditions develop.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
